# `aitbc gpu-onchain allocate`

Record a GPU allocation on the blockchain for a client.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc gpu-onchain allocate [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--gpu-id` | text | — | yes | GPU ID to allocate |
| `--client-id` | text | — | yes | Client wallet address |
| `--duration-hours` | float | — | yes | Allocation duration in hours |
| `--total-cost` | decimal | — | yes | Total cost in AIT |
| `--wallet` | text | — | yes | Wallet name for signing |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |
| `--wait` | flag | `false` | no | Wait for the transaction to be mined |
| `--format` | choice | — | no | Output format |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc gpu-onchain allocate --gpu-id <gpu_id> --client-id <client_id> --duration-hours <duration_hours> --total-cost <total_cost> --wallet <wallet>
```
